name: 托马斯·斯特恩斯·艾略特

points.place: 美国密苏里州圣路易斯
points.title: 早年教育
points.description: 艾略特出生于圣路易斯的一个显赫家庭，祖父是创立华盛顿大学的威廉·艾略特。他在哈佛大学接受教育，广泛接触哲学、文学和多种语言。这一时期，他深受法国象征主义诗歌和印度哲学的影响，开始创作早期诗歌。圣路易斯的保守环境与艾略特后来追求的欧洲现代主义形成鲜明对比，塑造了他对传统与现代关系的思考。
points.descriptionEn: Born into a prominent family in St. Louis, with his grandfather being William Eliot who founded Washington University. He received education at Harvard University, where he was exposed to philosophy, literature, and multiple languages. During this period, he was deeply influenced by French Symbolist poetry and Indian philosophy, beginning to write early poetry. The conservative environment of St. Louis contrasted sharply with the European modernism he would later pursue, shaping his thoughts on the relationship between tradition and modernity.

points.title: 欧洲求学
points.description: 艾略特前往巴黎索邦大学学习哲学，同时接触先锋艺术和文学。在这里，他结识了让·莫雷亚斯等象征主义诗人，并深受法国现代主义影响。巴黎的艺术氛围激发了他的创作灵感，他开始探索诗歌形式的革新。这段经历为他后来的现代主义诗歌创作奠定了基础，也使他形成了对欧洲文化的深厚认同，最终促使他决定移居英国。
points.descriptionEn: Eliot went to Paris to study philosophy at the Sorbonne while also engaging with avant-garde art and literature. There, he met Symbolist poets like Jean Moréas and was deeply influenced by French modernism. Paris's artistic atmosphere inspired his creative work, and he began exploring innovations in poetic form. This experience laid the foundation for his later modernist poetry and fostered his deep identification with European culture, eventually leading him to decide to move to England.

points.title: 文学生涯起步
points.description: 移居伦敦后，艾略特在银行工作，同时积极参与文学圈。1915年发表《J·阿尔弗雷德·普鲁弗洛克的情歌》，确立了他的现代主义诗人地位。1922年，他创办文学杂志《标准》，并发表代表作《荒原》，这部作品被誉为20世纪最具影响力的诗歌之一。在伦敦，他与庞德、伍尔夫等现代主义作家密切交往，形成了独特的创作风格，将欧洲传统与当代破碎感相结合，开创了现代主义诗歌的新方向。
points.descriptionEn: After moving to London, Eliot worked in a bank while actively participating in literary circles. In 1915, he published 'The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock,' establishing his status as a modernist poet. In 1922, he founded the literary magazine 'The Criterion' and published his masterpiece 'The Waste Land,' considered one of the most influential poems of the 20th century. In London, he closely interacted with modernist writers like Ezra Pound and Virginia Woolf, developing a unique style that combined European tradition with contemporary fragmentation, pioneering new directions in modernist poetry.

points.title: 皈依与成熟
points.description: 1927年，艾略特正式加入英国国教，这一转变深刻影响了他后来的创作。他开始探索宗教与文学的关系，创作了《灰星期三》等宗教主题作品。同时，他的文学批评理论逐渐成熟，在《传统与个人才能》等文章中提出了一系列重要文学观点。这一时期，他成为英国知识界的重要人物，对现代文学批评产生深远影响。他的诗歌风格也从早期的实验性转向更加传统与宗教性的表达，但保留了现代主义的技巧。
points.descriptionEn: In 1927, Eliot formally converted to Anglicanism, a transformation that profoundly influenced his later work. He began exploring the relationship between religion and literature, creating religious-themed works like 'Ash Wednesday.' Simultaneously, his literary criticism theory matured, with essays such as 'Tradition and the Individual Talent' presenting significant literary perspectives. During this period, he became an important figure in British intellectual circles, exerting profound influence on modern literary criticism. His poetic style also shifted from early experimentation toward more traditional and religious expression, while retaining modernist techniques.

points.title: 晚年荣誉
points.description: 1948年，艾略特因《四个四重奏》获得诺贝尔文学奖，表彰他对现代诗歌的革新贡献。晚年，他继续创作诗歌和戏剧，包括《鸡尾酒会》等作品。1957年与瓦莱丽·弗莱彻结婚，度过相对平静的晚年。作为文化评论家，他对西方文明衰落表达了深切忧虑，主张回归传统价值。艾略特晚年成为英国文坛的标志性人物，其作品被广泛研究，影响持续至今。1965年在伦敦逝世，被葬于西敏寺诗人角，与英国文学巨匠为邻。
points.descriptionEn: In 1948, Eliot was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for 'Four Quartets,' recognizing his innovative contributions to modern poetry. In his later years, he continued writing poetry and plays, including works like 'The Cocktail Party.' In 1957, he married Valerie Fletcher and enjoyed a relatively peaceful later life. As a cultural critic, he expressed deep concern about the decline of Western civilization, advocating a return to traditional values. In his later years, Eliot became a iconic figure in British literature, with his works widely studied and his influence continuing to this day. He died in London in 1965 and was buried in Poets' Corner at Westminster Abbey, resting alongside other British literary giants.

supporter.zh: 艾略特被誉为现代主义诗歌的奠基人之一，他的《荒原》彻底改变了20世纪诗歌的面貌。支持者认为他成功地将欧洲传统与当代经验融合，创造了独特的诗歌语言。他的文学批评理论强调传统的重要性，对后世批评家影响深远。艾略特后期作品中的宗教探索展现了他对精神世界的深刻思考，为现代文学注入了新的维度。他被视为文化保守主义的代表，但同时又是最具创新精神的现代诗人，这种矛盾统一构成了他独特的艺术成就。
supporter.en: Eliot is hailed as one of the founders of modernist poetry, with 'The Waste Land' revolutionizing the landscape of 20th-century verse. Supporters argue he successfully merged European tradition with contemporary experience, creating a unique poetic language. His literary criticism theory emphasizing tradition's importance has profoundly influenced later critics. The religious exploration in his later works demonstrates his deep contemplation of the spiritual realm, injecting new dimensions into modern literature. He is seen as a representative of cultural conservatism while simultaneously being one of the most innovative modern poets, this paradoxical unity constituting his unique artistic achievement.

critic.zh: 批评者指出艾略特的诗歌过于晦涩难懂，充满了复杂的典故和碎片化的意象，使普通读者难以接近。他的文化保守主义立场被批评为精英主义和反民主，对现代社会的变革持消极态度。艾略特对传统文化的推崇有时被视为对进步思想的阻碍，他的反犹言论和种族观念也备受争议。此外，他的诗歌中流露出的对现代文明的悲观态度，被批评为缺乏建设性，只提供诊断而不提供解决方案。这些批评认为艾略特虽然艺术成就卓越，但其思想观念存在明显的历史局限性。
critic.en: Critics point out that Eliot's poetry is excessively obscure, filled with complex allusions and fragmented imagery that make it inaccessible to ordinary readers. His cultural conservative stance has been criticized as elitist and anti-democratic, holding a negative attitude toward societal change. Eliot's reverence for traditional culture is sometimes seen as an obstacle to progressive thought, and his anti-Semitic remarks and racial views have also been controversial. Additionally, his pessimistic attitude toward modern civilization in his poetry is criticized as lacking constructive elements, offering only diagnosis without solutions. These critics argue that while Eliot achieved remarkable artistic accomplishments, his ideological perspectives contain significant historical limitations.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，艾略特被定义为一位复杂的现代主义文化符号，既是革新者又是传统主义者。他的作品成为理解20世纪西方精神危机的重要文本，被广泛研究于文学课程中。艾略特的影响超越了文学领域，延伸到文化批评、宗教思想和哲学讨论。他的诗歌语言和意象已成为流行文化中的常见引用，影响着后来的音乐、电影和艺术创作。尽管他的某些观点受到质疑，但艾略特作为文化转型时期的关键人物的地位得到普遍认可，他的作品持续为当代读者提供思考现代性、传统与信仰关系的丰富资源。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Eliot is defined as a complex modernist cultural symbol, both an innovator and a traditionalist. His works have become essential texts for understanding the spiritual crisis of 20th-century Western civilization and are widely studied in literature courses. Eliot's influence extends beyond literature into cultural criticism, religious thought, and philosophical discourse. His poetic language and imagery have become common references in popular culture, influencing later music, film, and artistic creation. Although some of his views have been questioned, Eliot's status as a key figure in a period of cultural transformation is widely recognized, and his works continue to provide contemporary readers with rich resources for contemplating modernity, tradition, and faith.

self.zh: 人类无法承受太多的现实。
self.en: Human kind cannot bear very much reality.

others.zh: 艾略特是我们这个时代最伟大的诗人，也是最具有影响力的文学批评家之一。他的作品不仅改变了诗歌的面貌，也改变了我们思考世界的方式。
others.en: Eliot is the greatest poet of our time and one of the most influential literary critics. His work has not only changed the face of poetry but also the way we think about the world.
